content.text:
I submitted **index 5 (Sb fraction 0.467)** as the best composition, with an EQE of **0.0104%**. That was the highest of the five compositions I measured. All five EQE measurements were used; I used one of the five XRD measurements.

| Index | Sb fraction | EQE (%) |
|---|---|---|
| 2 | 0.353 | 0.0012 |
| **5** | **0.467** | **0.0104** |
| 6 | 0.505 | 0.0060 |
| 11 | 0.689 | 0.0018 |
| 15 | 0.805 | ~0 (−0.0001) |

- **Where the peak is:** EQE is highest at Sb fractions of about 0.45–0.5. Moving from index 6 to index 5 (toward the copper-rich end) almost doubled it. It falls off steeply toward the antimony-rich end and on the copper-rich side at 0.35.
- **Why I looked there:** The XRD pattern of index 6 matches CuSb₂O₆ best (similarity 0.64), with extra features that suggest excess copper. The purer CuSb₂O₆ at index 11 (Sb 0.69) performed poorly. So the active material looks like CuSb₂O₆ with extra copper, not the stoichiometric compound.

The true peak could be at index 4 (Sb 0.428), which I never measured, since EQE was still rising when I stopped. The score only counts measured compositions, so the result stands at index 5's value.
